intent.idea: Explain why popcorn pops, and why a few kernels in every bowl never do, through the kernels themselves changing on screen rather than a labelled machine.
intent.audience: curious adults and teens scrolling short vertical video
intent.intended_effect: a satisfying 'oh, that's why' about the unpopped kernels at the bottom of the bowl, plus one surprising fact about the pop sound

premise.title: Two Kernels, One Crack
premise.opening_image: The bottom of a bowl of popcorn seen in cross-section: under the fluffy heap, two hard kernels that never popped.
premise.audience_hook: Why do a few kernels in every bowl never pop?
premise.central_action: Two identical-looking kernels heat side by side in a pan, cut open like a diagram: water inside both turns to steam, one hull holds it until it bursts into foam and jumps, the other has a hairline crack and hisses its steam away.
premise.complication: The kernels look the same from outside; the difference is a crack too small to notice until the steam finds it.
premise.payoff: The flake lands in the bowl and the leaky kernel ends up at the bottom, answering the opening question; a replay of the burst shows the pop is the steam rushing out.

intent.logline: Two kernels heat in one pan; the sealed one bursts into a flake and jumps, the one with a hairline crack leaks its steam and ends up at the bottom of the bowl.
intent.opening_promise: A cross-section of a popcorn bowl reveals two hard kernels at the bottom, with the question of why they never popped.
intent.ending: The flake drops into the bowl, the camera sinks to the bottom, and the dry cracked kernel lies there among the unpopped: their steam got out.
intent.style: Risograph science zine: off-white paper, overprinted flat inks (blue linework, fluorescent pink, yellow) with 3-unit misregistration, halftone dot shading, paper grain; cutaway diagrams instead of characters.

audio_intent.music: original note-list score synthesised in code
audio_intent.sfx: seeded procedural sound design on the moment table

shot_plan.sees: a cross-section bowl of popcorn; the camera sinks to two hard kernels at the bottom
two kernels in a cold pan open like a diagram: soft starch, blue water drops, a hard shiny hull that glints
the flame lights, the thermometer passes 100 °C, water drops boil into bubbles; in the sealed kernel bubbles crowd and the hull bulges and trembles
the camera finds a hairline crack in the right kernel; steam hisses out of it in a plume, its bubbles drain away and its hull relaxes and browns
the thermometer reaches 180 °C; the sealed hull splits, petals of hull fold back and white starch foam blooms out in slow motion; a leg of starch presses the pan and the kernel jumps
a replay of the burst: the hull cracks silently, then the steam jet bursts out and sound rings spread from the jet
the flake drops into the bowl and the camera sinks to the bottom where the dry cracked kernel lies

hardest_shot.why: The burst must look like real popcorn forming (hull splitting, foam lobes blooming into a recognisable flake) and the leg-kick jump must read as a physical push on the pan; a generic white blob or a cut would lose the payoff.
hardest_shot.fallback: Stage the burst as a cut from a straining kernel to a fully formed flake mid-air with a sound accent, and drop the leg line.
